title: GraphLake: A Purpose-Built Graph Compute Engine for Lakehouse
by: Shige Liu, Songting Chen, Chengjie Qin, Mingxi Wu and Jianguo Wang (Purdue University, TigerGraph), arXiv
summary: Explains why running graph analytics over Iceberg tables is hard and how a TigerGraph-based engine does it: load only the key columns that form the topology, build one edge list per Parquet file, encode file and row in each vertex ID so properties can be fetched on demand, and cache column chunks with graph-aware priorities. On LDBC benchmarks it reports up to 26× faster startup and up to 60× faster queries than PuppyGraph, and it is candid that edge-list scans lose to TigerGraph’s own storage when few edges match. Half the authors work at TigerGraph and the baseline is a closed-source competitor measured from outside, so read the comparison with that in mind.
